title: Java Throw
learningObjectives: Use throw to raise an exception explicitly.
Use throws to declare possible checked exceptions.
Create and throw standard exception types.
Define a simple custom exception class.
Choose exception messages that help callers recover.

understand.concept: Java uses throw to raise a particular exception object at a point where a rule is violated. A method declaration uses throws to state that a checked exception may escape to its caller. These keywords serve different purposes. You can throw standard exceptions such as IllegalArgumentException or define a custom exception to describe a domain-specific failure.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic equips Java learners to write robust programs using java throw in real applications.
understand.analogy: Think of each language feature as a clearly labelled tool: choose it for the specific problem it is designed to solve.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the Java language and library contracts; compile and test the actual behaviour.

explain.narrative: Validate method arguments close to the method boundary and throw IllegalArgumentException for invalid caller input. A checked custom exception can extend Exception; callers must catch it or declare it. An unchecked custom exception can extend RuntimeException. Avoid using exceptions for ordinary branching or hiding programming errors. Include a concise message that explains what condition failed.

examples.title: Throw for a negative age
examples.code: public class Main { static void checkAge(int age) { if (age < 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Age cannot be negative"); } public static void main(String[] args) { try { checkAge(-2); } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) { System.out.println(e.getMessage()); } } }
examples.explanation: throw raises the supplied exception object immediately.

examples.title: Declare a checked exception
examples.code:
import java.io.IOException;
public class Main { static void verify(boolean ok) throws IOException { if (!ok) throw new IOException("Verification failed"); } public static void main(String[] args) { try { verify(false); } catch (IOException e) { System.out.println(e.getMessage()); } } }
examples.explanation: throws declares the checked exception that the caller must handle.

examples.title: Throw an arithmetic exception
examples.code: public class Main { static int percentage(int value) { if (value < 0) throw new ArithmeticException("Value must be non-negative"); return value; } public static void main(String[] args) { try { percentage(-1); } catch (ArithmeticException e) { System.out.println("Rejected"); } } }
examples.explanation: A method can explicitly raise a standard unchecked exception.

examples.title: Custom exception
examples.code:
class InvalidCodeException extends Exception { InvalidCodeException(String message) { super(message); } }
public class Main { static void validate(String code) throws InvalidCodeException { if (code.length() != 4) throw new InvalidCodeException("Code must have four characters"); } public static void main(String[] args) { try { validate("AB"); } catch (InvalidCodeException e) { System.out.println(e.getMessage()); } } }
examples.explanation: A custom checked exception communicates a domain-specific failure.

examples.title: Propagate to caller
examples.code:
import java.io.IOException;
public class Main { static void load() throws IOException { throw new IOException("Unavailable"); } public static void main(String[] args) { try { load(); } catch (IOException e) { System.out.println("Handled by main"); } } }
examples.explanation: The exception propagates until a caller handles it.

practise.guidedTask: Build a small Java program that demonstrates java throw. Predict the output before compiling with JDK 21.
practise.independentTask: Create a practical application using java throw. Include at least two test cases, expected output, and an explanation of one important edge case.
hints: Start with the smallest standard Java API or language construct that expresses the requirement.
Trace the execution path and verify the documented behaviour of each method or keyword.
Compile with JDK 21 and test normal as well as boundary or failure cases.
practise.challenge: Extend one example into a small reusable component and document its error handling, ordering or concurrency guarantees as relevant.

questions.explanation: throw explicitly raises an exception at runtime.

questions.prompt: What does throws do in a method signature?
questions.answer: Declares exceptions that may be propagated
options: Declares exceptions that may be propagated
questions.explanation: throws documents and declares possible exceptions for callers.

questions.prompt: Which standard exception is commonly used for invalid method arguments?
questions.explanation: IllegalArgumentException signals an unacceptable argument value.

questions.prompt: What should a custom checked exception extend?
questions.explanation: A checked custom exception can extend Exception directly.

questions.prompt: What must a caller do when a method declares a checked exception?
questions.answer: Catch it or declare it with throws
options: Catch it or declare it with throws
questions.explanation: Java requires checked exceptions to be caught or declared.
